item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q022_colg_crya_remote_homology","answer":"In SCOPe 2.04 the ColG collagen-binding domain from PDB 1nqd and the C-terminal, domain-III beta-sandwich of Cry3A from PDB 1dlc were not asserted to be homologs: they were kept as different superfamilies despite both being all-beta beta-sandwich/jelly-roll domains. In current SCOPe they have been promoted to the same homologous superfamily within the same all-beta fold, while remaining separate families, so the supported claim is remote common ancestry rather than close family membership. The structural basis is the shared two-sheet jelly-roll/galactose-binding-domain-like core and the same topology across the conserved beta-strand scaffold; the functional support is that both domains are noncatalytic bacterial surface-binding modules, with ColG using this domain to bind collagen and Cry3A domain III contributing to receptor or carbohydrate recognition in the insecticidal toxin. That common binding role is evidence for ancestry of the domain scaffold, but it is not enough to transfer detailed specificity or activity: Cry3A should not be annotated as a collagenase domain, the ColG collagen-binding domain should not be treated as a Bacillus Cry toxin domain, and either structure is at most a remote template for the conserved beta-sandwich core rather than for loops, binding residues, substrate specificity, or toxicity.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
